articles.title: South Korea Moves to Establish Low-Carbon Standards for K-Pop Concerts
articles.summary:
Efforts to establish common standards for reducing carbon emissions at K-pop concerts are gaining momentum. The initiative involves management agencies, concert venues, production companies, ticketing platforms, and energy, transportation, and waste management entities working together to measure carbon emissions across the entire concert lifecycle and develop reduction strategies. On December 8, the inaugural policy debate for the "Consultative Body for Establishing Carbon-Neutral Concert and Event Guidelines," hosted by the office of Representative Lee Jung-moon of the Democratic Party of Korea and the K-pop climate action platform Kpop4Planet, was held at the Members' Office Building of the National Assembly in Yeouido, Seoul. Government and public institutions, concert planning and production companies, venue operators, private associations, and experts attended to discuss measures for measuring and managing concert carbon emissions. The consultative body plans to hold a total of five meetings through February next year.

This consultative body is significant because it connects eco-friendly efforts previously conducted by individual agencies, concerts, or festivals into industry-wide common standards. Concerts involve multiple stakeholders, from management agencies to venues, production companies, stage installation firms, ticketing platforms, transportation providers, energy suppliers, waste management companies, and audiences. Without consistent methods to measure where and how much carbon is emitted at each stage, it is difficult to set reduction targets. The consultative body plans to first accumulate measurable data, discuss reduction measures and support policies by sector, and then translate these into guidelines.

The Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism (MCST) has also begun securing baseline data. Kim Yu-mi, head of the Popular Culture Industry Division at the MCST, said assessing the current situation must come first to create guidelines, and that they plan to pilot a carbon emission calculator for the concert and event sector next year. The Korea Creative Content Agency (KOCCA) is conducting a beta test of the carbon emission calculator centered around HYBE, SM, and JYP, as well as concert venues in the Seoul and Incheon regions.

In the field, cost and infrastructure issues were cited as major challenges. Han Moon-gyu, CEO of Sound Alliance, which hosted the eco-friendly festival "Sustainable Wave Festival" at the Incheon Munhak Stadium last August, stated that continuous measurement is necessary so producers can understand what can be reduced. Concerns were also raised that the guidelines could function as de facto regulations, with industry figures proposing standards be established centered around venues and facilities instead of uniform rules.

articles.title: Figure Skater Cha Jun-hwan to Star in Roy Kim's 'Sparkle' Music Video Ahead of Acting Return
articles.summary:
The teaser for Roy Kim's "Sparkle" music video features figure skater Cha Jun-hwan and Seo Soo-min having a chance encounter in a bookstore.

The two play a young man and woman who gradually grow closer by passing notes between books. Cha is gearing up for his official acting debut. After starting his career as a child actor, he gained fame as a figure skater before being cast as the lead in the upcoming tvN sitcom "Gungjeon Land." Marking his return to acting after a long hiatus, he will showcase his acting skills through the music video first.

His co-star, Seo Soo-min, made her name known by playing So Ji-sub's daughter in the SBS drama "Director Kim," which wrapped up its run in July. This marks the first time Cha and Seo are working together in a project. In the teaser, the two express their emotions without dialogue, focusing on their gazes, facial expressions, and gestures.

"Sparkle" is a signature song by the Japanese band RADWIMPS, well known as the soundtrack for the animated film "Your Name." As the fourth release in Roy Kim's "J-POP REMAKE" project, "Sparkle" will be released on various music streaming sites at 6 p.m. on the 11th. The full music video starring Cha Jun-hwan and Seo Soo-min will also be unveiled on the same day.

articles.title: Singer Sung Si-kyung's Outdoor Concert Draws Complaints Over Operations Amid Praise for His Response
articles.summary:
Singer Sung Si-kyung held his "2026 Sung Si-kyung with Friends [Now, Today]" concert on May 5 and 6 at the 88 Lawn Garden of Seoul Olympic Park. Launched in 2022 and previously held indoors, the concert was moved outdoors for the first time this year.

Following the event, concertgoers shared mixed reviews about the venue's operations online. One attendee voiced frustration, writing that despite the 160,000-won ticket price and a 6 p.m. showtime, they had to line up by 11 a.m. and enter at 2 p.m., sweating under the blazing sun. Attendees complained that long waits for food resulted from an insufficient number of food trucks for the crowd size, and that there was a lack of adequate shade and separate waiting areas.

Meanwhile, Sung received praise for his on-site response. Concerned that fans who arrived early would be exhausted from the wait, he took the stage before the main concert, performing a duet with Kim Kwang-jin, with Kim Jang-hoon also joining for a surprise performance. As operational complaints persist, neither the organizers nor Sung's agency have released an official statement.

articles.title: Vice Justice Minister Says Leak of Prosecution Documents in Han Dong-hoon Case Constitutes a Crime
articles.summary:
Vice Justice Minister Lee Jin-su said on Jan. 9 that an indictment plan report regarding nominee Kim Seung-won, which was made public by independent lawmaker Han Dong-hoon, "is highly likely an internal prosecution document that was leaked." Speaking during a parliamentary interpellation session at the National Assembly, Lee added that providing investigative materials constitutes a crime under the leakage of official secrets and the Personal Information Protection Act.

Responding to a question by Democratic Party lawmaker Jeon Yong-ki regarding how lawmaker Han obtained the Seoul Western District Prosecutors' Office indictment plan document, Lee stated that internal reports produced during the prosecution's decision-making process must not be leaked under any circumstances. Jeon and other Democratic Party leadership members have pointed out that Han has been illegally acquiring and distributing prosecution investigative materials.

On Dec. 4, Han wrote on Facebook that the Western District Prosecutors' Office had decided to indict nominee Kim and delivered an indictment plan to the Supreme Prosecutors' Office and the Ministry of Justice, asking who blocked the indictment and why.

Asked whether the investigative team may have leaked the materials, Lee said that possibility cannot be ruled out, noting both current and former officials are subject to punishment for leaking secrets. Lawmaker Jeon criticized the situation, saying the prosecution must not become a political tool, and called for a special counsel investigation if structural leaks are confirmed.

articles.title: Koo Kyo-hwan Gears Up for Action: 'Resurrected Man' Cast to Hit Theaters from Release Day through Holidays
articles.summary:
"Resurrected Man: The Red" follows Seok-hwan (played by Koo Kyo-hwan), an unemployed job seeker whose only qualification is groundless self-confidence, as he discovers he has the ability to resurrect 72 hours after death and finds himself the target of a mysterious pursuit.

On the release date of the 30th, Koo Kyo-hwan, Shin Seung-ho, Kang Ki-young, Kim Si-a, and the director will attend stage greetings starting at CGV Yongsan I'Park Mall, followed by Megabox COEX and Lotte Cinema World Tower. Stage greetings will continue on National Foundation Day, Oct. 3, at additional theaters including CGV Yeongdeungpo Times Square and Lotte Cinema Yeongdeungpo.

On Oct. 5 during the holiday period, the cast will meet audiences at CGV Yongsan I'Park Mall, CGV Wangsimni, Lotte Cinema Konkuk University, Megabox COEX, and Lotte Cinema World Tower.

articles.title: ChatGPT Cements Role as Business Tool as OpenAI Strengthens South Korea Strategy
articles.summary:
Marking the first anniversary of the launch of its South Korea office, OpenAI is stepping up its push into the domestic enterprise artificial intelligence (AI) market. The company's strategy is to expand ChatGPT from a simple work assistant into an enterprise productivity platform capable of independently handling research, analysis, development, and automation.

Domestic weekly active users for ChatGPT Work and Codex grew about 14-fold over the six months starting in March. Codex is a coding agent that supports writing, editing, and reviewing code, while ChatGPT Work applies Codex's agent technology to ChatGPT to handle everything from research and analysis to document creation.

OpenAI Korea General Manager Kim noted that AI use among domestic companies has expanded across legal, sales, finance, marketing, and operations functions, citing Samsung Electronics and Seoul National University as organizations building AI use across their entire operations. OpenAI also plans to expand its "Partner Network" with major system integrators, cloud specialists, and AI startups, and to broaden model access through platforms such as Amazon Bedrock.

Since June 19, OpenAI has served ads to adult ChatGPT users in South Korea, reaching a $1 billion annualized ad revenue run rate in under 200 days.

articles.title: Comedian Lee Hyuk-jae Booked for Drunk Driving After Rear-Ending Motorcycle
articles.summary:
Lee Hyuk-jae's blood alcohol concentration measured between 0.03% and 0.08%, a level warranting a license suspension. Police plan to review whether to additionally apply charges of bodily injury resulting from professional negligence, pending confirmation of the victim's injuries.

Lee debuted in 1999 as an open-recruitment comedian for MBC and gained fame through entertainment programs such as "Star Golden Bell." However, he suspended his entertainment activities following a controversy in January 2010 involving an assault on a room salon employee, and has since faced a series of controversies, including lawsuits over unpaid debts in 2015 and 2017, and being placed on the National Tax Service's list of high and habitual delinquents last year.

articles.title: Public-Private Body Formed to Create K-Pop 'Low-Carbon Concert' Guidelines
articles.summary:
A public-private-industry-academia consultative body has been launched to establish low-carbon guidelines for the K-pop industry, aiming to induce carbon reduction across the performance sector by setting standards to manage carbon emissions generated during concerts.

K-pop4Planet, a climate crisis response platform for K-pop fans, held a launch ceremony and policy debate on the "Consultative Body for Establishing Carbon-Neutral Concert and Event Guidelines" at the National Assembly Member's Office Building in Yeongdeungpo-gu, Seoul, on Dec. 8. Concerts are considered the largest source of greenhouse gas emissions in the music industry, with carbon generated not only by stage energy use but also audience and artist travel, and production and waste disposal.

Lee Ji-eun, a senior researcher at Shin & Kim, said that in the K-pop industry, where overseas tours are active, the capacity to measure and manage carbon emissions can become a competitive edge, and that carbon neutrality should be approached as a strategy to enhance industrial competitiveness beyond mere regulatory compliance.

Participants voiced the urgent need to secure data for measuring concert carbon emissions and establish common standards, citing difficulties in gathering information on audience travel, venue energy use, and subcontractor data.

articles.title: Son Ye-jin, Ji Chang-wook, and Nana Bring Dangerous Desires to Netflix's 'Scandals'
articles.summary:
A press conference for the new Netflix series "Scandals" was held on the 9th at the JW Marriott Dongdaemun Square in Jongno-gu, Seoul. Director Jung Ji-woo and actors Son Ye-jin, Ji Chang-wook, and Nana attended the event to share details about the project.

"Scandals" is an eight-part series that depicts a bold and dangerous love wager between Lady Cho (played by Son Ye-jin), a woman of exceptional talent constrained by the limitations of the Joseon era, and Joseon's ultimate romantic, Cho-won (played by Ji Chang-wook), alongside the story of Hui-yeon (played by Nana), a woman entangled in their bet. Based on French author Pierre Choderlos de Laclos's novel "Dangerous Liaisons" and adapted to the Joseon Dynasty, the series is directed by Jung Ji-woo.

Son Ye-jin, who plays Lady Cho, said her desire to work with Director Jung and curiosity about the character led her to join the project. Ji Chang-wook said the emotions and relationships in the classic novel were extremely interesting, and that reinterpreting it as a 2026 series was intriguing. Nana said she has long admired the director and felt she could express the character Hui-yeon well.

Director Jung praised all three actors, saying Son Ye-jin carries the story like a superhero, that Ji Chang-wook brought humor to an affectionate character, and that Nana stepped away from traditional images with great strength.

articles.title: How Did 2024 Korean Thriller 'Your Honor' Become a Netflix Hit in 2026?
articles.summary:
The Korean legal thriller "Your Honor" became a Netflix hit in 2026 after joining the platform in August and reaching No. 1 on Netflix's series chart six days later. The series, originally broadcast on ENA as a Genie TV original in August 2024, drew renewed attention two years after its debut, reflecting changing streaming habits where older titles can resurface through algorithms, word of mouth, and actor popularity.

The drama stars Son Hyun-joo and Kim Myung-min as two men who abandon law and justice to protect their sons. The psychological duel between the fathers was singled out as the show's main appeal when it first aired, and it went viral even with the limited reach of a Genie TV original.

Director Yoo Jong-sun said on social media that the ranking was stunning and thanked actor Heo Nam-jun and fans for the late resurgence. Heo Nam-jun's later success in SBS's "Brave New World" is credited with helping drive new viewers back to "Your Honor."
